newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil income distribution improves with Real Plan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil income distribution improves with Real Plan.

text.p: Income distribution in Brazil improved last year, particularly after the Real anti-inflation plan introduced in July 1994, newspapers said today.

Newspapers said a survey published by the National Statistics Institute (IBGE), the first carried out by the institute after the Real Plan, showed the poorest 10 percent of the population accounted for 1.1 percent of the country's total wealth in 1995, up from 0.7 percent in 1993.
The Real Plan knocked monthly inflation down to one percent from 50 percent.
That means a record since the Cruzado stabilization Plan in 1986, when the poorest accounted for one percent.
The monthly average income of Brazilian workers rose 29 percent to 433 reais from 336 reais in 1995, when compared with 1993, papers said.
Despite the slight improvement, Brazil continues to be among the countries with the worst distribution of income in the world, newspapers said.
